verdict.rationale: Penpot documents a public backend RPC API. The hosted instance serves a machine-readable OpenAPI 3.0.0 document with 152 paths and a Swagger UI, the integration guide points developers to the auto-generated API reference, and access tokens let an app authenticate against it. The probe 404s on help.penpot.app do not contradict this, because the spec lives on design.penpot.app. Missing for 10: hand-written narrative API guides beyond the auto-generated reference, API docs on by default for self-hosted instances (they sit behind a flag), and independent hands-on reports of driving Penpot through the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Penpot's hosted SaaS instance serves a machine-readable OpenAPI 3.0.0 document for the backend RPC API (152 paths, server design.penpot.app/api/main/methods).
The integration guide directs developers to "the backend API documentation, generated automatically from source code, as a guide"
Use access tokens as an alternative login authentication. They can allow an app to access Penpot's API.
The hosted instance serves a Swagger UI page ("MAIN API") that loads the live OpenAPI document from /api/main/doc/openapi.json.
